adoption.body: Current AI use increased slightly to 23.8% of businesses, while expected use within six months rose to 27.6%. The gap narrowed to 3.8 percentage points, putting stated near-term intentions closer to reported deployment. Adoption remains uneven: the leading sector's current-use reading rose materially to 49.0%, more than twice the all-business rate.
adoption.headline: Business AI use rises as the near-term intention gap narrows

compute.body: Computer and peripheral-equipment output grew 9.2%, with capacity utilization at 81.7%. Semiconductor and electronic-component output grew 11.5%, but utilization was lower at 72.2%. Output is rising in both industries, while the utilization gap indicates different pressure on installed capacity.
compute.headline: Compute output is growing under different capacity conditions

connectivity.body: Public records list 168 active U.S. internet exchange points with 2,805 combined reported members. They also list 90 U.S. international submarine cable systems and 115 U.S.-connected cable catalog entries. Morningstar reported that Ekinops is supporting Bluebird Fiber's Midwest network investments, a regional example of continued network investment. Neither the national counts nor that project report establishes available bandwidth or redundancy in a specific data-center market.
connectivity.headline: Exchange points and subsea cables give the U.S. a broad interconnection footprint

economic_impact.body: Nonfarm-business productivity grew 2.2% as real output rose 2.5%. Real hourly compensation increased 0.6%, while unit labor costs grew 1.4%, indicating positive aggregate performance without a comparable increase in real compensation. A report that investors are pricing in a 32.6% AI productivity boost for software engineers describes an expectation for a specific workforce segment, not an economy-wide result. The current aggregate data do not identify AI's contribution.
economic_impact.headline: Productivity is rising, but compensation gains remain modest

finance.body: The Chicago Fed NFCI stands at -0.49 after a 0.02 increase over three months. Borrower strain is 26.0, compared with lender strain of -13.5, leaving a pronounced split beneath the aggregate measure. Morningstar reported that AI financing partnerships are credit-positive for Nvidia and data-center operators. That assessment points to benefits for the named participants, not uniformly easier financing for borrowers.
finance.headline: The NFCI increases amid a wide borrower-lender strain gap

grid_storage.body: Electric-power construction growth increased materially to 10.8%. The active interconnection queue stands at 2,061 GW, and only 24.2% is in executed-agreement or construction stages; storage accounts for 552.7 GW of the queue. S&P Global reports that data centers are adding to transmission congestion. Faster construction is a meaningful counterweight, but most requested capacity has not reached an advanced stage.
grid_storage.headline: Grid construction accelerates while most queued capacity remains at early stages

macro.body: Investor support remains constructive but selective. The AI Equity Index edged up to 36.7 and the median one-year return reached 13.7%, while the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns fell to 62.7%. The Financial Times reported that robust AI spending was supporting expectations for another strong U.S. earnings season, but the return data still show uneven participation. Financing is also mixed: the NFCI is -0.49 after a 0.02 rise over three months, while borrower strain is 26.0 and lender strain is -13.5. Computer and peripheral-equipment output is growing 9.2%, and semiconductor and electronic-component output 11.5%. Commercial electricity demand growth of 3.1% is also outpacing total retail demand growth of 1.2%. These are broad industry measures rather than AI-only series, but they describe an expanding hardware and power context for the buildout. Grid execution remains separate from the size of the pipeline: only 24.2% of the active interconnection queue is in executed-agreement or construction stages. Utility Dive reported that MISO proposed fast-track studies for large loads and generation. The proposal is a procedural change, not delivered capacity. Broader diffusion is less evident in labor and business use. Only one tracked AI-linked labor channel has positive employment growth, led by power and communication construction at 0.8%, and two have positive real-earnings growth. CNBC reported surging Wall Street AI hiring, which provides a sector-specific contrast rather than evidence of broad acceleration. Current AI use is reported by 23.8% of businesses, with 27.6% expecting use within six months. These measures leave diffusion through firms and the labor market incomplete even as selected industries report strong AI hiring.
macro.headline: Market support and physical expansion coexist with narrow labor gains

market.body: The AI Equity Index edged up to 36.7 and the median one-year return rose to 13.7%, but the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns slipped to 62.7%. Gains therefore persisted without becoming more broadly distributed. The Financial Times reported that robust AI spending was supporting expectations for another strong U.S. earnings season. That strengthens the near-term earnings narrative, but it does not show that results are improving across the full set of covered companies.
market.headline: AI shares advance without broader participation

workforce.body: Only one tracked AI-linked labor channel has positive employment growth. Power and communication construction leads at 0.8%, while two channels have positive real-earnings growth. CNBC reported that Wall Street AI hiring is surging, providing a sector-specific counterpoint. The report does not amount to broad acceleration across the tracked labor channels.
workforce.headline: Sector-specific AI hiring contrasts with narrow tracked job growth

editorial_briefing.style_reference: AI Macro is a research platform that examines the development of the U.S. AI economy from capital investment and physical construction through deployment, adoption, and economic results. It uses publicly available data to relate corporate and market activity to the physical systems required to support the buildout. It evaluates the extent to which that investment produces durable economic value and how its effects are transmitted through the broader U.S. economy.

body.text: The AI Equity Index slipped to 36.0, but the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns rose to 64.2% and the median return increased to 16.4%. Average sector trading pressure also edged up to 50.5. The broader return distribution contrasts with the lower index reading. Reuters reported that AI-related companies were expected to drive most third-quarter U.S. earnings gains; that supports near-term expectations but does not yet establish realized gains across the full group.

headline.text: Return breadth improves despite a softer AI index

body.text: Operating cash flow is 1.42 times current capital expenditure, while cash reserves are equivalent to 0.96 years at the current spending rate. The first ratio shows current spending covered by ongoing cash generation; the second puts cash on hand alone at just under one year of current CapEx. At the same time, borrower strain is 26.0 and lender strain is -13.5. The split argues against treating adequate internal coverage as evidence of uniformly easy external finance.

headline.text: Internal cash generation exceeds current CapEx, but borrower and lender strain diverge

body.text: The active interconnection queue contains 2,061 GW, including 552.7 GW of storage, but only 24.2% has reached executed-agreement or construction stages. Just 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation. Recent PJM developments moved in different directions: the operator approved fast-track interconnection for 2.1 GW, while FERC rejected most of its large-load interconnection plan. The actions place a project-level approval alongside a setback for the broader large-load framework.

headline.text: Most queued grid capacity remains far from advanced stages

body.text: Businesses expecting to use AI within six months rose slightly to 27.7%, but the expected-minus-current use gap also widened slightly to 3.9 percentage points. The leading sector's current-use reading reached 50.2%, and BTOS now reports a current-use reading for every sector. A separate 2025 Small Business Credit Survey found that 46% of firms with employees said their business or employees used AI tools, with another 15% planning adoption within twelve months. Because its population, wording and horizon differ from BTOS, it is a complementary measure rather than a directly comparable adoption rate.

headline.text: Near-term intentions edge further ahead of current AI use
Investment support persists as grid execution and broad diffusion remain uneven

paragraphs.text: Current investment remains covered by operating cash flow, and public-market returns have broadened, but the financing picture is not uniformly easy. Operating cash flow is 1.42 times current CapEx and cash reserves equal 0.96 years of CapEx, while borrower strain of 26.0 contrasts with lender strain of -13.5. Among covered companies, 64.2% have positive one-year returns and the median return has risen to 16.4%, even as the AI Equity Index slipped to 36.0. Reuters reported that AI-related companies were expected to drive most third-quarter U.S. earnings gains, reinforcing the near-term earnings narrative rather than demonstrating broader economic gains.

Hardware output continues to expand, but the grid pipeline is much larger than its advanced portion. Computer and peripheral-equipment output grew 9.2%, and semiconductor and electronic-component output grew 11.5%. The active interconnection queue is 2,061 GW, yet only 24.2% is in executed-agreement or construction stages, and just 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation. In PJM, a 2.1 GW fast-track interconnection approval was followed by FERC's rejection of most of the region's large-load interconnection plan. These are distinct actions, but together they show why requested capacity should not be treated as a delivery schedule.

Business adoption is moving upward in BTOS, though other surveys measure different populations and forms of use. BTOS reports that 27.7% of businesses expect AI use within six months, 3.9 percentage points above current use, and the leading sector's current-use reading is 50.2%. A separate 2025 Small Business Credit Survey found that 46% of firms with employees said the business or its employees used AI tools and another 15% planned adoption within twelve months. The surveys provide complementary views rather than one directly comparable adoption rate.

Broad labor-market transmission is less evident. Only one tracked AI-linked channel has positive employment growth, led by power and communication construction at 0.8%, and two have positive real-earnings growth. At the economy-wide level, nonfarm-business productivity grew 2.2% and real output 2.5%, while real hourly compensation rose 0.6%. These are positive aggregate outcomes, but they do not identify AI's contribution or show broad transmission through employment and compensation.

editorial_synthesis.instructions:
You are writing the current research update for AI Macro.

Use only the findings and recent developments in the supplied briefing. Decide what matters, connect related evidence when the relationship is supported, and explain it in clear, natural English for an intelligent general reader. Prioritize significance over coverage. It is fine for the evidence to be mixed. Do not force unrelated facts into one story.

The style reference shows the desired level of restraint, specificity, and sentence construction. Match those qualities without copying its wording. Write like a careful human analyst. Use concrete subjects and verbs. Avoid rhetorical gimmicks and artificial-sounding transitions. Do not mention the prompt, the briefing, evidence IDs, validation, methodology, or the writing process.

On a normal update, candidate_domains identifies sections that may deserve replacement. Update only the domain Reads for which you can write something materially more useful than the prior publication; you may return no domain Reads when none deserves replacement. On a bootstrap publication, write every candidate domain because no prior Read exists. Always write one new Macro Read that explains the most important current story across the platform in two to four coherent paragraphs.
